info.title: Let's Seal signing service
info.description:
The Let's Seal signing service is the keyed core of Let's Seal — the open standard
for sealing anything, self-hostable and free. *The "Let's Encrypt for documents."*

Open standards, end to end:

* **PAdES / X.509** for the cryptographic seal (via pyHanko + an on-prem CA)
* **OpenTimestamps** for a free Bitcoin anchor proving a file existed by a date
* **SHA-256** everywhere; hash-only endpoints so a file never has to leave the caller

**Trust is self-anchored.** A proof stands on the published root, open standards,
and the public blockchain — authenticity anyone can verify, backed by a published
root.

⚠️ **Runs localhost/private only — it holds signing keys.** The public, rate-limited
surface lives in the app tier in front of it.

post.summary: Issue a business signing certificate
post.description: Issue a signing certificate for a new business (runs the CA script).

post.summary: Render a proof QR (PNG)
post.description: Render a QR code (PNG) for a proof URL — used to stamp sealed PDFs.

post.summary: Sign a client CSR under a profile
post.description:
CA-as-code: sign a client-supplied CSR under a signing profile.

The client generates and keeps the private key; we only sign the CSR. Trust
is self-anchored (our CA isn't in OS/vendor trust stores) — verify via the
chain + the portal, not automatic OS trust. Profiles: document | code | data.

post.summary: Seal a PDF
post.description: Seal an uploaded completed PDF with the org's signing cert.

200.description: The sealed PDF. `X-Letsseal-Sha256` and `X-Letsseal-Cert-CN` headers carry the digest and signer.

post.summary: Detached CAdES/CMS seal over a file digest
post.description:
Seal ANY file: a detached CMS signature over its SHA-256, chaining to the
root. Digest-only — the file never leaves the caller. Pair with `/anchor/hash`
for the Bitcoin timestamp; together they are the full SEAL for a non-PDF.

post.summary: Verify a detached CAdES/CMS seal
post.description:
Verify a detached seal: the file's bytes + its `.sig`, against our root.
Powers the public portal for any non-PDF artifact.

post.summary: cosign-compatible signature over a file digest
post.description:
Seal an artifact for the supply-chain lane: a raw ECDSA-P256 signature over
its SHA-256 plus the org's codeSigning leaf cert, in cosign's flat
signature+certificate form. Digest-only — the artifact never leaves the caller.
Verifies with `sealbot verify`, `openssl`, and stock `cosign verify-blob`.

post.summary: Verify a cosign-format blob signature
post.description:
Verify a supply-chain blob seal: the artifact's bytes + its base64 `.sig` +
the signer's `.pem` (leaf, optionally with chain), against our root.

get.description:
The identity providers this service is configured for (those with an OAuth
client id set). The web tier reads this to render only the sign-in buttons
that will actually work.

post.summary: Seal a digest under a provider-verified identity
post.description:
Verify a Google/GitHub/OIDC proof, mint a short-lived leaf binding the
provider-verified email, and sign the artifact's SHA-256 with it. Digest-only
— the artifact never leaves the caller. Verifies with `sealbot verify` and
stock `cosign verify-blob --certificate-identity <email>`.

We never assert identity ourselves: the seal records that the *provider*
verified the signer's control of that email at seal time.

post.summary: Verify an identity seal
post.description:
Verify an identity seal: the artifact's bytes + its base64 `.sig` + the
signer's `.pem`, against our root — and surface WHO signed (the verified
email) and WHO vouched (the OIDC issuer recorded at issuance).

post.summary: Sign a DSSE/in-toto attestation (SBOM / provenance) over a digest
post.description:
Sign an in-toto/DSSE attestation binding a predicate (SBOM, SLSA provenance,
vuln scan) to an artifact's SHA-256, with the org's codeSigning leaf. Digest-only
— the artifact never leaves the caller. The returned `bundle` verifies with stock
`cosign verify-blob-attestation --bundle att.bundle --key signer.pub --type <type>
--insecure-ignore-tlog`, and with `sealbot` via the cert chain to our root.

post.summary: Verify a DSSE/in-toto attestation
post.description:
Verify a supply-chain attestation: the artifact's bytes + its DSSE `bundle`
+ the signer's `.pem`, against our root — and confirm the attestation's subject
digest matches the uploaded artifact (claims check).

post.summary: Sign a transparency-log Signed Tree Head
post.description:
Sign a Signed Tree Head with the system log key. Internal — the web app
owns the log and computes the root; this authenticates it.

get.description:
The log signing cert + chain (public, no key). Published so STH signatures
are self-verifiable.

post.summary: Seal an image with an embedded C2PA manifest
post.description:
Embed a C2PA (Content Credentials) manifest signed by the org cert into an
image, chaining to the same root. The image is rewritten (the manifest lives
inside it), so the bytes are uploaded; time comes from a separate anchor.

200.description: The signed image (Content Credentials embedded). `X-Letsseal-Sha256`, `X-Letsseal-Cert-CN` and `X-Letsseal-Format` headers carry the digest, signer and MIME.

post.summary: Verify an image's embedded C2PA manifest
post.description: Verify an image's embedded Content Credentials against our root.

post.summary: Seal an XML document with an enveloped XML-DSig signature
post.description:
Embed an enveloped W3C XML Signature signed by the org cert into an XML
document, chaining to the same root. The document is rewritten (the signature
lives inside it); time comes from a separate anchor on the signed bytes.

200.description: The signed XML (enveloped signature embedded). `X-Letsseal-Sha256` and `X-Letsseal-Cert-CN` headers carry the signed-document digest and signer.

post.summary: Verify an XML document's enveloped XML-DSig signature
post.description: Verify an XML document's enveloped signature against our root.

post.summary: Seal an email message with an S/MIME signature
post.description:
Wrap a mail message in a standards-conformant S/MIME `multipart/signed`
envelope signed by the org cert, chaining to the same root. Same CMS crypto as
the detached seal, delivered in the form mail clients speak.

200.description: The signed message as a `multipart/signed` .eml. `X-Letsseal-Sha256` and `X-Letsseal-Cert-CN` headers carry the signed-message digest and signer.

post.summary: Verify an S/MIME signed email message
post.description: Verify an S/MIME `multipart/signed` message against our root.

post.summary: Verify a sealed PDF
post.description: Verify an uploaded PDF against our CA — powers the public portal.

post.summary: Anchor a file on Bitcoin
post.description: Anchor sha256(pdf) on a decentralized ledger. Returns the proof.

post.summary: Anchor a bare digest on Bitcoin
post.description: Anchor a bare SHA-256 digest on a decentralized ledger (no file upload).

post.summary: Upgrade a pending anchor
post.description:
Given an existing .ots proof (base64), try to upgrade it to a confirmed
Bitcoin attestation. Returns the (possibly updated) proof + status.

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the artifact the attestation is about.

org_slug.title: Org Slug
org_slug.description: Issuing business slug (must have a code-signing cert).

predicate.title: Predicate
predicate.description: The claim object: an SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), SLSA provenance, vuln scan, etc.

predicate_type.title: Predicate Type
predicate_type.description: Short type (spdxjson|cyclonedx|slsaprovenance|vuln|custom) or a full predicateType URI.

subject_name.title: Subject Name
subject_name.description: Human name for the subject (informational; the digest is what's bound).

csr.title: Csr
csr.description: PEM-encoded PKCS#10 CSR. The client keeps the private key.

legal_name.title: Legal Name
legal_name.description: Legal entity name to embed in the cert subject.

data.title: Data
data.description: Payload to encode (typically a proof URL).

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file to seal.

org_slug.title: Org Slug
org_slug.description: Issuing business slug (must have a signing cert).

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the artifact to seal.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: OIDC provider id: google | microsoft | apple | github | <configured>.

token.title: Token
token.description: The provider's proof: an OIDC ID token (JWT) for OIDC providers, or a GitHub OAuth access token for provider=github. Verified here against the provider before any cert is minted.

tree_size.title: Tree Size
tree_size.description: Number of leaves the head covers.

ts.title: Ts
ts.description: Timestamp (ms) the head is signed at.

sealed.title: Sealed
sealed.description: Whether a PAdES signature was found at all.

intact.title: Intact
intact.description: The WHOLE document is unaltered since sealing (covered bytes untouched AND nothing appended after the signature).

covered_intact.title: Covered Intact
covered_intact.description: Raw: only the bytes within the signature's range are unmodified (does NOT account for content appended after signing).

whole_document.title: Whole Document
whole_document.description: The signature covers the entire file (no incremental updates after it).

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: Signature coverage level: ENTIRE_FILE (good) | ENTIRE_REVISION | CONTENTS_ONLY | ...

trusted.title: Trusted
trusted.description: Chains to this CA's trust root.

authentic.title: Authentic
authentic.description: AUTHORITATIVE pass/fail verdict: valid AND intact AND trusted. A valid signature from an unrecognized (self-signed) cert is NOT authentic. Render verdicts from this, not sealed/intact alone.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why verification could not proceed (when unsealed).
